title: Sprint 1: Public Noticeboard, External Recipients & Full Scope Delivery
goal: Re-integrate the public noticeboard with Trident likes, broaden recipient support for external emails with single-use guest unlock links, build the Dev SuperPeek inspector, and enforce full end-to-end testing for every issue.

issues.title: [Feature] Public Noticeboard Feed & Trident Salute System
issues.user_story: As a user or guest, I want to browse anonymously shared letters that have reached their delivery date and salute them with Trident likes, so I can be inspired by letters sailing across time.
acceptance_criteria: Letter model includes visibility enum ('private', 'public_anonymous', 'public_named') and likes integer.
GET /api/letters/public returns only delivered public letters, excluding sealed or private letters.
Noticeboard supports sorting by: 'recent', 'most_liked', and 'long_journey'.
Public anonymous letters mask sender name/avatar and show a random pirate alias (e.g., 'Ghost of Jaya').
POST /api/letters/:id/like increments the like count and is rate-limited to prevent spam.
Noticeboard is accessible to unauthenticated guests and authenticated users.
end_to_end_test_plan: 1. [API Test] Create Letter A (visibility: 'public_anonymous', deliveryDate: past). Force deliver letter. Query GET /api/letters/public -> verify Letter A is returned with sender details redacted.
2. [API Test] Create Letter B (visibility: 'private', deliveryDate: past). Query GET /api/letters/public -> verify Letter B is NOT returned.
3. [UI Test] Navigate to /noticeboard in an unauthenticated incognito window. Verify masonry feed loads public letters.
4. [UI Test] Click the Trident (🔱) salute button on a card -> verify counter increments with micro-animation and state persists on refresh.
5. [Automated] Add test assertion to server/src/scripts/smoke.js validating public feed filtering and like increment.

issues.title: [Feature] Arbitrary External Recipient Flow & Guest Unlock Link
issues.user_story: As a sender, I want to write and seal a letter to any email address (even if they do not have an account), so they receive a single-use unlock link to view their treasure chest without mandatory registration.

services: server/src/services/emailService.js (format guest unlock URL in delivery email)
client_components: client/src/components/letter/RecipientPicker.jsx (add 'Other Nakama' email input, 'Add to Crew' checkbox)
client_pages: client/src/pages/TreasureChest.jsx (support guest unlock view with register CTA)

acceptance_criteria: RecipientPicker allows switching between: 'Myself', 'My Partner' (if paired), and 'Other Nakama (Any Email)'.
When sent to an external email, a cryptographically secure UUIDv4 unlockToken is generated.
On delivery, the email sent via Resend contains a direct link: `${CLIENT_URL}/unlock/${unlockToken}`.
Accessing `/unlock/:token` displays the delivered letter with full 3D chest reveal without requiring auth.
Guest reveal page displays a friendly 'Join the crew to seal your own letters' banner.
If 'Add to Crew' was checked, recipient is added to sender's crewMembers array in MongoDB.
end_to_end_test_plan: 1. [API Test] POST /api/letters with recipientEmail 'guest.friend@domain.com' -> verify unlockToken is generated.
2. [API Test] Force deliver letter -> verify delivery email logs link with unlock token.
3. [UI Test] In incognito window (no auth cookie/token), navigate to /unlock/<token> -> verify chest opening animation plays and reveals content.
4. [Security Test] Verify that querying an invalid or expired token returns a clean 404 seafaring error page ('Lost at Sea').
5. [Automated] Include guest unlock assertion in server/src/scripts/smoke.js.

issues.title: [Feature] Admin SuperPeek & Dev Letter Inspector
issues.user_story: As a developer or tester in local/staging environments, I want an admin SuperPeek tool to inspect sealed letters without altering database delivery dates, so I can verify content formatting and debugging workflows.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/dev/peek/:id returns the full unredacted letter body regardless of delivery date ONLY when ENABLE_DEV_ROUTES=true.
In production environments (NODE_ENV=production), dev routes are completely disabled and return 404.
In local client dev mode, Captain's Log displays a 'SuperPeek' badge/button on sealed cards allowing instant preview.
Quick 'Force Deliver' and 'Trigger Sweep' buttons are accessible from the Dev Inspector Bar.
end_to_end_test_plan: 1. [API Test] Create a letter sealed 5 years in future. Call GET /api/dev/peek/:id with valid dev token -> verify unredacted body is returned.
2. [Security Test] Set ENABLE_DEV_ROUTES=false -> call /api/dev/peek/:id -> verify HTTP 404.
3. [UI Test] In local dev mode, click 'SuperPeek' on a sealed letter in /log -> verify letter modal previews body without marking letter as delivered.
4. [Automated] Validate dev route toggle in server smoke tests.

issues.title: [Feature] Pirate Rank Progression & Bounty Showcase
issues.user_story: As a user, I want my pirate rank and bounty to level up on my Wanted Poster as I seal letters across the Grand Line, so I feel rewarded for writing time capsules.

client_components: client/src/components/layout/Navbar.jsx (display rank badge next to avatar)

acceptance_criteria: Bounty and title tier rules: 0 letters = 'Landlubber' (฿0), 1-3 = 'Rookie Pirate' (฿1,000,000), 4-10 = 'Sea Dog' (฿50,000,000), 11-25 = 'Warlord of Letters' (฿300,000,000), 26-50 = 'Yonko Scribe' (฿1,000,000,000), 51+ = 'Pirate King' (฿1,500,000,000).
User profile in MongoDB updates bounty and pirateTitle automatically when letters are created.
Profile Wanted Poster features a golden animated bounty counter and pirate title ribbon.
Navbar displays pirate title and badge.
end_to_end_test_plan: 1. [API Test] Register new user -> verify initial bounty is 0 and rank is 'Landlubber'.
2. [API Test] Create first letter -> verify user document updates to 'Rookie Pirate' with ฿1,000,000 bounty.
3. [UI Test] Navigate to /profile -> verify Wanted Poster renders username, avatar, pirate rank, and formatted bounty.
4. [Automated] Add rank calculation unit test in server test harness.

issues.title: [Security & Reliability] 24-Hour Edit Lock & End-to-End Suite
issues.user_story: As a sender, I want clear feedback that my letter is locked once it is within 24 hours of delivery, so I know it is actively sailing and cannot be tampered with.

client_pages: client/src/pages/WriteLetter.jsx (lock status banner and disabled fields)

acceptance_criteria: Letters within 24 hours of deliveryDate return HTTP 423 Locked for GET /:id/edit, PATCH /:id, and DELETE /:id.
UI displays locked status badge with tooltip: '⚠️ This letter is within 24 hours of delivery and is sealed for voyage.'
Smoke test suite exercises 100% of auth, pairing, lock window, bullmq, sweep, and reveal paths.
All npm run smoke assertions pass.
end_to_end_test_plan: 1. [API Test] Create letter 12 hours from now. Attempt PATCH /api/letters/:id -> verify HTTP 423 response.
2. [API Test] Attempt DELETE /api/letters/:id -> verify HTTP 423 response.
3. [UI Test] Open /write/:id/edit for locked letter -> verify inputs are disabled and banner informs user.
4. [Automated] Run npm run smoke -> verify all checks pass cleanly.
